text.p: The launch of the space shuttle Columbia was postponed on Tuesday for 24 hours because a coolant pipe was not properly insulated, NASA said.

Columbia's blastoff had been scheduled for Thursday afternoon but engineers feared the pipe, located at the front end of the shuttle's cargo bay, might freeze and burst in the cold vacuum of space, said Bruce Buckingham, a spokesman for the U.S. space agency NASA.
Fuel loaded aboard Columbia earlier on Tuesday was being drained and workers expected to open the shuttle's payload bay before dawn on Wednesday to wrap the pipe in insulating blankets.
If all goes according to plan, liftoff would be rescheduled for 1:07 p.m. EST (1807 GMT) on Friday, Buckingham said.

NASA timed the launch earlier in the day to allow a daylight landing in Africa should an emergency occur. A device need for night touchdowns at the shuttle's emergency landing strip at Banjul in Gambia was not working.
The shuttle was to spend 16 days aloft while a crew of seven performed dozens of microgravity experiments in the fields of combustion research and materials science.
